questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code invalidates cached agent queues when tickets change? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
An unassigned ticket (assigneeId null) has its status set to solved. What does setStatus do to the cache?
choices: It throws because a null key is passed to Redis
It makes no Redis call, because invalidate filters out the null id and skips DEL when no keys remain
It writes an empty queue for the null agent

questions.prompt: Agent X escalates one of their tickets to urgent. When does X's queue reflect the new ordering?
choices: On X's next agentQueue call, which misses the cache and re-sorts from the repo
Never, the cached order is kept until the ticket is solved
Immediately, because escalate rewrites the cached array in place

questions.prompt: Why does this design invalidate (delete) the queue rather than update the cached array on each ticket change?
choices: Deleting avoids re-implementing filtering and sorting on each write; the next read rebuilds the queue from the repo
Deleting guarantees no reader can ever observe stale data
Updating in place would require a longer TTL
